title: Movie Studios Promote Films by Just Giving Away Money
summary:
Promoting a movie in the internet age usually means memes, influencer screenings and wild popcorn buckets. But two studios have tried a simpler trick: just dangling money in front of people.

The marketing teams behind "How to Rob a Bank," from Amazon MGM Studios, and "Ebenezer," from Paramount Pictures, both used cash giveaways ahead of their shared November 13 release in North American theaters.

For the heist thriller "How to Rob a Bank," a branded ATM was moved between movie theaters around Los Angeles over four days. Fans who followed the film's social media channels could find clues to the machine's location and a PIN number, which would trigger a payout of a single one-hundred-dollar bill.

"Ebenezer" took a cheekier approach. The studio promoted an official Venmo account for its main character, the famously penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge from Charles Dickens's classic tale. Users could request money from the account — and those who scrolled through its transactions found it shared Scrooge's spirit: the only completed payouts were single cents.

The Venmo account was only active for a few hours, though Paramount teased followers to "check back," saying "Ebenezer might be feeling generous on Venmo again."

Both stunts fit their films' themes: "Ebenezer" is about a miser who catches the Christmas spirit, while "How to Rob a Bank" follows thieves who teach subscribers how to take money back from banks.

There was also an unexpected twist: the Venmo account could receive payments from users, not just send them. One fan, Krystyna Ursta of Los Angeles, said she sent about $30 and received a full refund a few days later — plus an extra penny and an invitation to a special screening in New York. A person familiar with the account said all money received was sent back privately.
why_it_matters: Stunts like these show how hard companies compete for attention online — and why fans should read the fine print before sending money to a promotion.
